info.bio:
Elastica fue un grupo inglés enmarcado en el Britpop, famoso por su música pegadiza y angular, influenciada por el punk rock. Son conocidos por su álbum Elastica de 1995, un éxito comercial y crítico tanto en el Reino Unido como en otros países.

La banda fue creada a mediados de 1992 por Justine Frischmann y Justin Welch, quienes habían tocado efímeramente en Suede y Spitfire; incorporándose posteriormente, en el otoño de ese año mismo año, Annie Holland y Donna Mathews (ex Darling Buds).

scenes.name: Brit-pop y post-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Como tantas veces, el fenómeno más publicitado es el menos interesante: un «brit-pop» de grupos terriblemente parecidos y tediosos, sin apenas imaginación. Lo anticipan Lightning Seeds, La's, Teenage Fanclub y Heavenly; estalla con Boo Radleys, Blur (Parklife) y Oasis (el «farol» que mejor personifica la moda). Suede y el glam-pop (Super Furry Animals, Placebo), las excepciones de High Llamas (Hawaii) y Supergrass, el revival mod (Ocean Colour Scene, Wildhearts), Elastica, Sleeper, las Spice Girls; Trembling Blue Stars, Tindersticks, Delgados. El post-pop de Radiohead, «la banda más publicitada y sobrevalorada de la década», cuyo OK Computer es una obra maestra del falso vanguardismo; Coldplay, Travis.

mentions.author: Piero Scaruffi
mentions.text: …Shriekback's bassist Dave Allen, Elastica, fronted by Justine Frischman and harking back to Blondie's and the Cars' disco-punk sound of the 1970s on Elastica (1995), Sleeper, also relying on a female voice (Louise Wener) on Smart (1995), offered a less trivial kind of commercial rock. The ultimate product…

podcast.title: Trainspotting Soundtrack Contribution (1996)
podcast.body: Elastica contributed to the first *Trainspotting* soundtrack in 1996. This soundtrack gained widespread acclaim and is often listed among the best movie soundtracks of all time, known for its mix of old and new rock and electronic music that captured the film's desperate yet uplifting tone. "New Order, Pulp, Blur, Underworld, Elastica, Lou Reed."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Admission of "Nicking" Wire's "Three Girl Rumba"
podcast.body: Justine Frieshmund, the leader of Elastica, openly admitted to being a big fan of Wire and deliberately taking elements from their 1977 song "Three Girl Rumba" for Elastica's song "Connection." This admission led to a settlement without a court case. "In fact, she admitted to being such a big fan that she deliberately nicked some of Three Girl Rumbaw for one of her songs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Admission of Influence and Theft
podcast.body: Justine Frischmann, the leader of Elastica, openly "admitted to being such a big fan" of Wire that she "deliberately nicks some of Three Girl Rumba for one of her songs," leading to royalties from Elastica's first album being awarded to Wire. Another song, "Waking Up," also led to a portion of the album's royalties being awarded to The Stranglers for similarity to their song "No More Heroes," categorizing it as "well-intentioned theft." "In fact, she admitted to being such a big fan that she deliberately nicks some of Three Girl Rumba for one of her songs, you know, as sort of a tribute or something."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Breakup of Britpop's "First Couple"
podcast.body: The relationship between Elastica's Justine Frischmann and Blur's Damon Albarn ended, "mostly over druck problems" (likely a transcript error for "drug problems"), leading to the dissolution of Britpop's unofficial "first couple." "Meanwhile, Justin and Damon all of our broke up, mostly overdruck problems."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Britpop Era Band
podcast.body: Elastica was a prominent band during the Britpop era of the mid-1990s, an era characterized by celebrating Britishness and acknowledging predecessors in British rock. "Elastica was one of the great bands of the Britpop era of the middle 1990s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Britpop Movement (Mid-to-Late 90s)
podcast.body: Elastica was a key band in the Britpop movement, which was a British response to American Grunge. "the British were still ringing out what they could from Britpop...you know Oasis and Blur and Elastakund swayed in all those bands."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Britpop Peak and Decline
podcast.body: Elastica made its debut in 1994 during the Britpop era, achieving massive success with their fastest-selling debut album in UK history. However, issues with drugs and "intrepid relationships" hindered the production of their second album, and by its release in 2000, Britpop had died off, leading to dismal sales and the band's amicable breakup. "Britpop had died off years earlier, the songs weren't there and sales were… well, dismal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Britpop's "First Couple"
podcast.body: Frontwoman Justine Frischmann's partnership with Damon Albarn of Blur positioned them as "the first couple of a moment" within the burgeoning Britpop scene, drawing significant media attention. "Justine was partnered out with Damon Albarn of Blur and together they essentially served as the first couple of a moment."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Britpop's "First Couple" (Damon Albarn & Justine Frischmann)
podcast.body: Elastica's frontwoman Justine Frischmann, formerly of Suede, was also Damon Albarn's girlfriend, leading to their unofficial designation as Britpop's "official first couple" and making them a media favorite. "Not only was she a former member of Swade, perfect, but she was also Damon Albarn's girlfriend. How awesome was that? Brit Pop had an official first couple."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall of Britpop

podcast.title: Britpop's First Couple
podcast.body: Frontwoman Justine Frischmann's relationships were a major media focus; she was a former member of Suede, a former girlfriend of Brett Anderson, and the current girlfriend of Damon Albarn of Blur, leading the media to declare them Britpop's "official first couple." "Britpop now had an official first couple."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Drug-Induced Inactivity
podcast.body: Most of the band, including leader Justine Frischmann, acquired heavy heroin habits, which severely hampered their ability to write or record a second album. "Most of the band had managed to acquire heavy heroin habits, including leader Justine Friespin."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Evaporation
podcast.body: After the Britpop era, Elastica "evaporated," unable to sustain their career amidst the challenges. "Lasted evaporated."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Heavy Heroin Habits & Creative Paralysis
podcast.body: Drug use was an even more severe issue for Elastica than Oasis, with most of the band, including leader Justine Frischmann, developing "heavy heroin habits" that prevented them from being able to write a second album. "Most of the band had managed to acquire heavy heroin habits, including leader Justin Frieshmann. They couldn't get it together long enough to write a second album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall of Britpop

podcast.title: Heroin's Impact and Band Decline
podcast.body: The band's potential was severely undermined by a major heroin addiction issue that "invaded the band." This led to a five-year delay in recording their follow-up album, by which time Britpop had faded, and the album was poorly received, ultimately resulting in the band's breakup. "The sad part of their story is that heroin invaded the band in a major, major way."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Justine Frischmann's Post-Elastica Career
podcast.body: After Elastica disbanded, Justine Frischmann collaborated with MIA, co-writing songs and achieving a hit. She also worked in television, married a professor of atmospheric science at the University of California Davis, and now works as a visual artist in San Francisco. "Justine wrote some songs with MIA and had a hit with her. She did a little TV and then she married a professor of atmospheric science at the University of California Davis."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lawsuits over Song Elements
podcast.body: Elastica faced two lawsuits, one from Wire and another from The Stranglers, for allegedly "nicking bits" of their older songs, highlighting the band's strong inspiration from 70s post-punk and new wave. "Elastica was such a fan of that music that they were sued twice once by Wire, a 70s post-punk band, and another time by the Stranglers for nicking bits of their old songs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Leading Britpop Band
podcast.body: Led by former architecture student Justine Frischmann, Elastica was one of the foremost bands of the Britpop era in England. "Over in England, Alaska led by former architecture student, Justine Friesman. They were one of the leading bands of the whole Britpop era."

podcast.title: Post-Britpop Dissolution
podcast.body: Elastica "evaporated" after the Britpop era ended, suggesting a complete disbandment or fading into obscurity without further significant activity. "Elastica evaporated."

podcast.title: Post-Music Career
podcast.body: Justine Frischmann transitioned from music to focus on painting and is currently married to a meteorologist and lives in Colorado. "She's now spending a lot of time painting and is married to a meteorologist in living in Colorado."

podcast.title: Rapid Fame
podcast.body: Elastica quickly achieved widespread fame, becoming "super famous super fast" even before the release of their debut album in 1995. "Elastica became super famous super fast even before they released their debut album in 1995."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Relationship Breakdown
podcast.body: Justine Frischmann and Damon Albarn (Blur) broke up, primarily due to drug problems, marking the end of the "Britpops first couple." "Meanwhile, Justine and Damon Oliver broke up mostly over drug problems."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Royalty Settlement with The Stranglers
podcast.body: The Elastica song "Waking Up" was deemed awfully similar to The Stranglers' 1977 song "No More Heroes." This resulted in a settlement where a portion of Elastica's first album royalties was awarded to The Stranglers, characterized as a clear case of "theft." "Same result. A piece of that first Elastica album was awarded to the Stranglers. Not an unfortunate son of coincidence, an actual case of... Well, theft."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Royalty Settlement with Wire
podcast.body: Following Justine Frieshmund's admission of similarity, Elastica settled with Wire by agreeing to surrender a certain amount of the royalties from their first album to Wire, in recognition of the homage paid to "Three Girl Rumba." "But damages had to be levied. And the ruling was that Elastica had to surrender a certain amount of the royalties from that first album to Wire."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Short, Sharp, and Fun Songs
podcast.body: Justine Frischmann was the singer, songwriter, and guitarist for the band, and their songs were characterized by their concise, incisive, and enjoyable nature. "Justine was the singer, the songwriter, and the guitarist. And the songs, they were short, sharp, and fun."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Similar to Oasis
podcast.body: Elastica was among the bands that started to appear, sounding similar to Oasis, demonstrating the latter's popularity and influence within the Britpop scene. "The Oasis approach proved to be so popular that they started to hear and see similar bands."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock: Chapter 12

podcast.title: Subsumed by Britpop
podcast.body: Elastica, along with many other bands tagged with the "new wave of new wave" label, was eventually integrated into the larger Britpop movement. "many of the bands tagged with that label were soon subsumed into something bigger that we call Brit Pop."

xref.title: Post-Music Artistic and Academic Pursuits
xref.body: After Elastica's breakup, Frischmann maintained a connection to music by helping her former roommate MIA develop her career. She also hosted two architecture series for the BBC, a subject she had studied previously. In 2005, she moved to Colorado to enroll in a master's program in visual arts at a Buddhist-inspired university, eventually becoming an acclaimed painter in San Francisco. "In 2005 she moved to Colorado, where she enrolled in a master's program in a small Buddhist inspired university to learn everything she could about visual arts."

xref.title: Transition to Pastoral Work
xref.body: After the breakup of Elastica, Donna Matthews left the music industry and entered the church, becoming a pastor. She dedicates a significant amount of her time to outreach work with the homeless. "Donna Matthews. C2 went into the church, becoming a pastor and works a lot with outreach to the homeless."
